title: Cucumber and BDD: Specs Everyone Can Read
description: What Behaviour-Driven Development is, how Cucumber turns plain-language Gherkin scenarios into automated tests, and how to keep a Cucumber suite readable, fast and trustworthy.
audience: Developers and testers new to BDD; examples use Java with Cucumber-JVM and JUnit 5.

chapters.title: Highlights
chapters.summary: The whole lesson in nine cards: the BDD conversation, Gherkin, glue, what goes wrong and the maths of a suite.

chapters.title: How Cucumber Fits Together
chapters.summary: From the BDD conversation to Gherkin, step definitions, the runner, hooks and reports, on one map you rebuild from memory.

chapters.title: Writing Good Scenarios
chapters.summary: Ten review decisions on real-looking scenarios: declarative steps, one behaviour each, Backgrounds, Outlines, tags and shared state.

chapters.title: Why Our BDD Failed
chapters.summary: A team adopted Cucumber and got slow, brittle tests nobody reads. Find out what really went wrong.

chapters.title: Suite Maths
chapters.summary: Play with flaky odds, retries, UI versus API steps, parallel runs and exploding Scenario Outlines.

chapters.title: Cucumber Archipelago
chapters.summary: One island per big idea, hands-on activities, then a final exam.

objectives: Explain how a BDD conversation becomes a Gherkin scenario and then an automated test
Write declarative scenarios that test one behaviour each and read like documentation
Diagnose why a Cucumber suite became slow, brittle or ignored
Estimate how flakiness, retries and Scenario Outlines change a suite's run time and trust
prerequisites: Some experience writing or reading automated tests

glossary.definition: Behaviour-Driven Development: agreeing on behaviour in concrete examples before writing code, then automating those examples.
The plain-language format of feature files: Feature, Scenario, Given, When, Then.
The code that runs for one Given, When or Then line; the glue between the scenario and the system.
A product, development and test person working out examples together before anything is built.
One scenario template run once per row of an Examples table.
Code that runs before or after each scenario or step, for set-up and clean-up.
A test that passes and fails without any change to the code, usually from timing, shared state or external dependencies.
Feature files that stay true because the suite runs them; the spec and the tests are the same text.
